english: My sibling wants to become a scientist when they grow up.
tip: 3rd-person wishes take -고 싶어해요: 되고 싶어해요 (doego sipeohaeyo = wants to become).

target: 방학 숙제를 아직 다 못 했어요.
english: I still haven't finished all my vacation homework.
tip: 못 + verb = 'cannot / didn't manage': 못 했어요 (mot haesseoyo = couldn't do).

english: My father watches the news every morning.
tip: 께서 (kkeseo) replaces 이/가 (i/ga) when the subject deserves respect: 아버지께서 보세요 (abeojikkeseo boseyo = father watches). The verb takes -세요 (-seyo) to match.

english: I'm very interested in economic news.
tip: Interest is something you have a lot of: 관심이 많아요 (gwansimi manayo) = 'interest is many'. 에 (e) marks its target – 경제 뉴스에 (gyeongje nyuseu-e) = in economic news.

english: I only read articles I'm interested in.
tip: 만 (man = only) follows the noun: 기사만 (gisaman = only articles).

english: When I read news comments I get angry.
tip: -(으)면 (-(eu)myeon) covers 'whenever', not just 'if': 읽으면 (ilgeumyeon) = when(ever) I read them. Habitual results like getting angry lean on it – no separate 'when' word.

english: I have over a hundred followers.
tip: 넘다 (neomda = to exceed) takes 이/가: 백 명이 넘어요 (baengmyeongi neomeoyo = over 100).

target: 저는 개인 정보를 온라인에 안 올려요.
english: I don't post personal info online.
tip: 안 + verb = negation: 안 올려요 (an ollyeoyo = don't post).

target: 저는 SNS 계정이 두 개 있어요.
english: I have two social-media accounts.
tip: 개 (gae) counts things with native numbers: 두 개 (du gae = two).

english: I switched my account to private.
tip: (으)로 marks a change-into: 비공개로 (bigonggaero = into private).

english: I subscribed to that channel right away.
tip: 구독하다 (gudokada = to subscribe) takes 을/를: 채널을 구독해요 (chaeneol-eul gudokaeyo).

target: 가족하고 주말에 영화를 세 편 봤어요.
english: I watched three movies with my family over the weekend.
tip: 편 (pyeon) counts films with native numbers: 세 편 (se pyeon = three films).

english: This drama has five seasons.
tip: 개 (gae) is the all-purpose counter for things, and low counts use native numbers: 다섯 개 (daseot gae) = five (seasons) – Sino 오 개 (o gae) would be wrong here.

english: When ads come on I get really annoyed.
tip: -(으)면 = 'when': 나오면 (naomyeon = when it comes out).

english: I look up videos of the singer I like.
tip: 의 (ui) shows possession: 가수의 영상 (gasu-ui yeongsang = the singer's video).

english: I study English on YouTube.
tip: (으)로 marks the tool: 유튜브로 (yutyubeuro = via YouTube).

english: I eat while watching mukbang.
tip: -(으)면서 = 'while': 보면서 (bomyeonseo = while watching).

target: 유료 웹툰은 미리 볼 수 있어요.
english: With paid webtoons, you can read ahead.
tip: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = 'can': 볼 수 있어요 (bol su isseoyo = can view).

english: That webtoon was made into a drama.
tip: (으)로 marks the result: 드라마로 (deuramaro = into a drama).

target: 번역 앱이 여행할 때 정말 유용해요.
english: A translation app is really useful when traveling.
tip: -(으)ㄹ 때 = 'when': 여행할 때 (yeohaenghal ttae = when traveling).

english: I set my alarm for six o'clock.
tip: 시 uses native numbers: 여섯 시 (yeoseot si = six o'clock).

english: My phone battery is already dead.
tip: 다 되다 = 'be all used up': 다 됐어요 (da dwaesseoyo = is dead/empty).

english: I left my charger at the hotel.
tip: -고 오다 = 'do and come': 두고 왔어요 (dugo wasseoyo = left it and came).

target: 저는 이메일을 하루에 스무 번 확인해요.
english: I check email twenty times a day.
tip: 번 (beon = times) uses native numbers: 스무 번 (seumu beon = twenty times).

english: I accidentally deleted an important file.
tip: (으)로 marks the cause here: 실수로 (silsuro = by mistake).

english: My parents find using new apps difficult.
tip: honorific of a 3rd-person feeling: 어려워하세요 (eoryeowohaseyo = find it hard).

english: Even abroad I watch Korean broadcasts on apps.
tip: -도 (-do = even/also): 해외에서도 (haeoeseodo = even abroad).

english: Thanks to the interpreter app, the conversation was easy.
tip: 덕분에 (deokbune = thanks to) follows a noun: 앱 덕분에 (aep deokbune = thanks to the app).

target: 저는 그 앱에 별점 오 점을 줬어요.
english: I gave that app five stars.
tip: 점 (jeom = points) uses Sino numbers: 오 점 (o jeom = five points).

english: This app is free, so it's really nice.
tip: 이다 connective -라서 = 'because it is': 무료라서 (muryoraseo = because it's free).
